lead: Digital World Acquisition / DWAC — top of the App Store, stuck in line
smaller: Lockheed Martin / LMT — the war trade finally gets its trigger
Ford Motor / F — exploring a split to borrow Tesla's multiple
3x Nasdaq 100 ETF / TQQQ — the YOLO dip-buy with triple leverage
why_lead: Repeat of the 21 February DWAC lead justified as a material update with newly published launch-day evidence (all 20-21 February): Reuters says Truth Social topped Apple App Store downloads while many users were waitlisted (n1610), Reuters on the app hitting the store (n1603), Forbes on a glitchy start and thousands waitlisted (n1613), Bloomberg on launch-day errors (n1623), CBS on a slow rollout (n1621), Forbes on Hannity and Greene joining (n1618), USA Today rating the $4.99-a-week claim false (n1611), The Independent on a British company's identical-logo legal threat (n1627) and Business Insider's 'peak stupid' professional mood piece (n0788). The 21 February lead was a pre-launch buy-the-rumour essay; this one is the post-launch scoreboard-versus-waitlist test, with a new analog (Coinbase's Super Bowl interest spike, n0869/n0883) instead of the Virgin Galactic round trip; Coinbase led the 15 February edition, so it appears here only as a supporting analog updated with the newly published Martin CEO critique (n0883). DWAC still shows its 84.32 USD 18 February close because of Presidents' Day, so Tuesday's open is the first price reaction. Earlier retail notes (1-16 February) never used DWAC.
why_smaller: Lockheed Martin: the war trade gets a new, concrete trigger after the 21 February edition, Putin's call to recognise the breakaway regions (Reuters n0218) and the troop order (Atlantic Council n1137); card shows LMT 386.46 USD, +4.11% 20s but -2.46% 5s, ITA -0.84% 5s and Rheinmetall -2.70% on 21 February, so the item is about a trade that has not yet worked. Defense contractors were not used in earlier retail notes (war-hedge items used Exxon on 2 and 8 February, GDX on 14 and 21 February and USO on 15 February).

Ford Motor: new sum-of-the-parts catalyst, the Los Angeles Times report that Ford's CEO is exploring ways to separate the EV business to unlock Tesla-like value (n1030), with F +2.85% on 18 February and a same-week spin-off template (Hasbro, n0593); breaks on Tesla's -9.21% 20s, Lucid's -29.56% and GM's president warning Musk about Tesla's pricing (n1719). Ford was not used in earlier notes; Rivian was a 15 February smaller item and appears here only as a card value, and the 21 February Tesla item (SEC fight) is a different narrative from Ford's sum-of-the-parts story.

TQQQ: the leveraged buy-the-dip / YOLO narrative supported by Yahoo Finance's YOLO piece (n0825), Fortune's 'how low can tech stocks fall' (n0803), A Wealth of Common Sense on crash recovery (n0781) and AdvisorHub's leveraged-ETF charge (n1587); TQQQ 50.44 USD, -3.39% 1s, -10.99% 20s, with VIX 27.75 and DAX -2.07% on 21 February as the Tuesday gap risk. Relation to earlier notes: TQQQ was a 4 February smaller item ('the leveraged dip-buy snaps back') and SOXL led on 16 February ('triple leverage on the peace rally'); this is a brief secondary material update built on newly published 17-21 February evidence (n0825, n0803, n0781, n1587) and a new trigger, the post-recognition Tuesday gap, rather than a rebound call.
considered_not_chosen: Bitcoin and altcoins (BTC 37,075.28 USD -3.53% on 21 February, SOL -8.56%, XRP -9.61%): the only market that traded through Putin's address, used as cross-asset backdrop in the lead rather than another crypto item (Bitcoin led on 8 and 14 February, Coinbase on 15 February, and Bitcoin was a smaller item on 4, 9 and 21 February; Solana was a 2 February smaller item).
Gold and GDX: unchanged US card values since the 21 February item, so no new price evidence to justify a carryover.
Polish banks (PEO -6.75%, MBK -6.00% on 21 February): large own-day drops but a nonretail Poland story with no retail-attention evidence.
DraftKings (-21.62% on 18 February), Roblox, Shopify: no new own-date catalyst after 21 February.
Home Depot (pending 22 February results; Reuters preview n1029): outcome unknown at cutoff and no retail-attention angle.

Avoided as possibly after the cutoff or superseded: n1270, n1283, n1292, n1293 (Biden agreeing in principle to a Putin summit, a diplomatic track overtaken by the recognition); no sanctions-tranche or Nord Stream headlines were used because those decisions fall on 22 February.
